abstract: BACKGROUND: Antidepressant selection is constrained by limited comparative-effectiveness data, with randomized trials measuring symptom reduction rather than patient-reported tolerability. We tested whether AI-assisted analysis of patient-written online reviews recovers drug-level tolerability signals that converge with the strongest randomized evidence. METHODS: We did a cross-sectional analysis of 8348 reviews of 16 antidepressants for major depressive disorder posted to Drugs.com (February 2008-March 2025; ≥1 month reported use). Two independent large language models (Claude Sonnet 4.5, Gemini 2.5 Pro) classified each review across 17 clinical dimensions using identical structured prompts; a stratified 100-review subsample (1700 classifications per reviewer) was independently rated by two experts, with all agreement statistics highly significant. We compared per-drug top-rating prevalence with Cipriani et al.'s 2018 network meta-analysis retention and efficacy odds ratios (Spearman correlation). RESULTS: Mean inter-LLM Cohen's κ was 0.81; expert reviewers agreed substantially with the dual-AI consensus (mean κ = 0.75 and 0.80). Top rating correlated strongly with Cipriani et al. retention odds ratios (ρ = +0.79, p < 0.001) but not with efficacy odds ratios (ρ = -0.14, p = 0.64). Within-SNRI heterogeneity was substantial. Emotional blunting was the strongest negative predictor of satisfaction (OR 0.20). LIMITATIONS: Reviews are from a single platform and self-selected users; drug-level comparisons rest on few agents; and the design is cross-sectional and ecological. CONCLUSIONS: AI-classified patient reviews recover the drug-level tolerability signal of randomized retention data and surface within-class heterogeneity, particularly among SNRIs, as a hypothesis-generating signal. Within the comparable-efficacy range of contemporary antidepressants, tolerability, especially emotional blunting, principally correlates with patient satisfaction.

title: Can AI-assisted analysis of antidepressant drug online reviewers (ADORE) inform real-world use of antidepressants?
